# SIGIL SARL

> Sovereign Integrity Governance Infrastructure Labs (SIGIL SARL) is a Cameroonian company based in Buea, Cameroon, building sovereign governance infrastructure for public institutions: systems where the institution holds the keys, the data stays under the institution’s control, and every consequential action is authorized, bounded, and proven. Founded and led by Junior Thuram Nana.

## Systems

- [VIGIL](https://sigilsovereign.com/systems/vigil/): Governed cybersecurity and evidence platform. Status: pilot. Source code: kept strictly private.
- [RÉCOR](https://sigilsovereign.com/systems/recor/): Sovereign beneficial-ownership registry. Status: pre-deployment. Source code: kept strictly private.
- [APEX](https://sigilsovereign.com/systems/apex/): Anti-corruption intelligence for public procurement. Status: pre-deployment. Source code: kept strictly private.

## Key facts

- Legal name: SIGIL SARL

- Trade register (RCCM): RC.BUA.2026.B.0190

- Contact: info@sigilsovereign.com

## Doctrine

- A technical capability is never an authorization.
- No finding is trusted until an independent, deterministic check re-verifies it.
- The institution always holds the keys and can read, export, and stop.
- Open standards over lock-in.

## System detail

### VIGIL

VIGIL is a cybersecurity platform that protects an organization’s systems, whether it is a public institution, a critical institution such as a bank, or a private company. It detects, observes, and blocks cyberattacks, and helps duly authorized operators find, confirm, remediate, and document vulnerabilities — under one rule: a technical capability is never an authorization. No model or agent can authorize itself, and no finding is trusted until an independent, re-verifiable check confirms it. Every observation stays a lead until an independent check confirms it as a fact, and each engagement closes with a tamper-evident dossier that re-verifies offline.

Standards: OWASP, MITRE ATT&CK, NIST 800-115, PTES, PASTA. Status: pilot. Source code: kept strictly private.

### RÉCOR

RÉCOR is a sovereign beneficial-ownership registry designed for Cameroon, built to satisfy FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 and to export to the Beneficial Ownership Data Standard (BODS v0.4). It was fully demonstrated to, and acknowledged by, Open Ownership on 1 July 2026.

Standards: FATF R.24, FATF R.25, BODS v0.4. Status: pre-deployment. Source code: kept strictly private.

### APEX

APEX reads public data — procurement notices, sanctions lists, corporate registries, court records, and citizen tips — detects defined patterns of procurement fraud, and scores each finding with a calibrated certainty engine. No single person can escalate a case: a five-member council, each holding a hardware key, must reach quorum, and every finding is independently verifiable against a public ledger without trusting the platform. It compiles evidence and signals confidence; a human institution makes every consequential decision.

Standards: UNCAC, OCDS. Status: pre-deployment. Source code: kept strictly private.

## Record

- 2026-04-09 — Presentation of APEX to UNDP Cameroon (Presentation of APEX). SIGIL presented APEX, its anti-corruption intelligence platform for public procurement, to UNDP Cameroon. A presentation is not an endorsement or a contract.
- 2026-07-01 — Open Ownership demonstration of RÉCOR (Technical demonstration of RÉCOR; acknowledged by Open Ownership). RÉCOR, built to the Beneficial Ownership Data Standard (BODS v0.4), was fully demonstrated to Open Ownership, which acknowledged the demonstration. This is a technical demonstration, not an endorsement.
- 2026-08-04 — Letter of appreciation, UNDP Cameroon (Letter of appreciation). UNDP Cameroon issued a letter of appreciation. A letter of appreciation is not an endorsement or a contract.
- 2026 — Invitation to present, APME (Invitation to present). APME (Small and Medium Enterprises Promotion Agency) invited SIGIL to present to its digitalization unit.
- 2026 — Meeting called by ANTIC’s Director General (Presentation of VIGIL; preparing for a full-scope evaluation). At the invitation of the Director General of ANTIC, Cameroon’s National Agency for Information and Communication Technologies, SIGIL presented VIGIL. SIGIL is now preparing for a full-scope evaluation by ANTIC. A meeting and an upcoming evaluation are not an endorsement or a contract.
- 2026-10-16 — CITS 2026 ecosystem roundtable (Invitation-only participation). SIGIL was invited to, and took part in, the CITS 2026 ecosystem roundtable: about 50 participants, by invitation only, held under the Chatham House Rule, bringing together development partners, government representatives, and other institutions. Taking part is not an endorsement or a partnership.
- 2026 — Paid pilot of VIGIL with DIGITT France (Paid pilot). VIGIL is in a paid pilot with DIGITT France. A pilot is bounded and agreed; it is not a production deployment or an endorsement.
- 2026-10-26 — Call with Open Ownership and UNDP Cameroon on RÉCOR’s next steps (Common objective and areas of work agreed). SIGIL, Open Ownership and UNDP Cameroon held a call on the next steps for RÉCOR. The participants agreed on a common objective and on the areas of work that will take RÉCOR from a developed system to a deployed one. A shared objective is not an endorsement or a contract.
